variables.reason: The candidate ledger defines Ra as the first-order absolute moment of surface-height fluctuations (mean absolute deviation). The cited KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness explicitly names Ra (symbols: Ra; R_a), gives the canonical quantity 'arithmetic mean roughness' with the definition 'Mean absolute deviation of surface height from its mean level' in the surface-roughness domain, and provides si_dimension L and dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]. This record therefore directly describes the same physical quantity used in the original problem (same name/symbol, same statistical meaning, same domain) and supports every exponent in the proposed SI vector (I=0, J=0, L=1, M=0, N=0, T=0, Theta=0).

The ledger's kt is defined as the peak-to-valley height (vertical distance between highest peak and lowest valley). The KB entry pq_peak_to_valley_height gives the canonical quantity 'mean peak-to-valley roughness height' with symbols including kt and the definition 'A roughness-amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences between peaks and valleys.' It lists si_dimension L and dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0], matching the candidate. The entry therefore applies directly to the kt in the original problem (same physical definition and symbol) and supports all SI exponents in the proposed vector.

The ledger defines k_rms as the root-mean-square height, the standard deviation of surface-height fluctuations. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height names k_rms (symbols: k_rms; krms), gives the canonical quantity 'root-mean-square roughness height' with the definition 'Root-mean-square fluctuation of surface height about its mean,' and provides si_dimension L and dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]. This record therefore documents the same physical statistic used in the problem and supports the full SI exponent vector proposed.

Sk in the ledger is the skewness of roughness-height fluctuations (third standardized moment). The KB entry pq_height_skewness defines 'surface-height skewness' with the symbol Sk, describes it as the third standardized moment of the surface-height distribution, and gives si_dimension 1 and dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0]. This record therefore directly applies to the ledger's Sk (same statistical definition and symbol) and supports the fully dimensionless SI exponent vector.

The ledger's Ku is defined as kurtosis (fourth standardized moment) of height fluctuations. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis gives the canonical quantity 'surface-height kurtosis' with symbol Ku, defines it as the fourth standardized moment of the surface-height distribution, and lists si_dimension 1 and dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0]. This directly confirms the ledger meaning and supports the candidate's dimensionless exponent vector.

ES in the ledger is the effective streamwise slope (mean absolute gradient of surface height). The KB entry pq_effective_surface_slope documents 'effective surface slope' with symbols ES and E_x, defines it as the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a specified horizontal direction, and explicitly notes that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is therefore dimensionless; its dimension_vector is [0,0,0,0,0,0,0]. This record therefore matches the ledger's ES both in definition and SI exponents and supports the proposed all-zero vector.

Po is surface porosity in the ledger. The KB record pq_porosity lists porosity with symbols Po and aliases, defines it as a fraction of void or open volume/area according to the chosen definition, and gives si_dimension 1 and dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0]. The record explicitly notes porosity is a dimensionless fraction and advises confirming the geometric definition; it applies directly to the ledger's Po and supports the candidate's dimensionless SI exponents.

gate.physical_correctness_scope: A passed contract is not a theorem of physical correctness. Record ID and coordinate checks establish citation consistency; semantic relevance/applicability in the reason and internal-reasoning physics remain model judgements.

variables.quantity_name: First-order absolute moment of height fluctuations
variables.physical_definition: First-order absolute moment of surface height fluctuations (mean absolute deviation of height).
Peak-to-valley height: vertical distance between the highest peak and lowest valley of the surface roughness.
Root-mean-square height: standard deviation of surface height fluctuations (measure of roughness amplitude).
Skewness of roughness height fluctuations: third standardized moment describing asymmetry of the height distribution.
Kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations: fourth standardized moment describing peakedness of the height distribution.

variables.quantity_name: Effective streamwise slope of the roughness
variables.physical_definition: Effective streamwise slope of the roughness: dimensionless measure of average incline of surface features in the flow direction.
Surface porosity: fraction of surface area (or volume) that is void; dimensionless.
